items.text: The biggest misread of anyone predicting the end of software engineering was imagining that the world only needed a certain amount of software, and bringing automation to the field would reduce the need for labor. Exactly the opposite is happening where essentially most things are actually turning into software. Because agents can use tools, work with computers, write software on the fly, and process data like humans (but far faster), we can now throw “software” at problems that never could reasonably be digitized before. items.text: To clarify: Replit remains model agnostic. Our users can choose Anthropic models as well as many other supported models. What I meant at TC Disrupt is that OpenAI is now our preferred partner powering Agent based on performance, cost, and strength of our partnership. We believe in giving our users model choice while optimizing the default experience for the best performance at the best price.

items.text: Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:06 What is a file system? It's a database. Right? Everything's a database. Speaker 1 | 00:06 - 00:15 It's the wild west for people that don't know their history databases. It's just like, you know, taking a cheetah, giving them much cocaine, and putting it a Ferrari. Like, the amount of speed that people are developing these things is insane. Speaker 2 | 00:16 - 00:38 That is Andy Pavlo. In the world of databases, Andy is about as close to a god as it gets. The Carnegie Mellon professor whose courses taught an entire generation of engineers about databases, and as it turns out, the AI models too.
